clue.text: See 14
Feller putting saddle on ass

indicators.note: putting one thing on another, in a down clue, places the first above the second
on means the first piece sits on top of the next in this down entry

parts.note: to saddle someone is to lumber them with a burden
a jack is a male donkey, as in jackass

explanation.surface: Someone is putting a saddle on a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' reads as a fellow, but it is one who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A lumberjack fells trees, so is literally a feller of timber.

clue.text: Irish booze Mike put in to change non-alcoholic cocktail

indicators.note: put in to means these pieces go inside the following word

parts.note: to change is to vary
gin is a kind of booze
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone spikes a drink with Irish liquor to alter it into a teetotal cocktail, which would defeat the purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The booze in the surface is a red herring: the drink being defined has no alcohol, and the gin only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Virgin Mary is a Bloody Mary made without vodka, so a cocktail containing no spirits.

clue.text: Sub rolling pass? I'm not sure

indicators.note: rolling turns the word over, so it is read backwards upward in this down entry

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
um is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: A substitute player is unsure whether to try a rolling pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a stand-in, especially a doctor substituting for another.

clue.text: Clear site to accommodate a building for display

parts.note: crystal clear: crystal means transparent

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so the following piece holds the other

parts.note: a site is a place

explanation.surface: Instructions to clear a plot so it can take an exhibition hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crystal Palace was the huge glass hall built for the Great Exhibition of 1851 in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crystal Palace was erected to house exhibits for the 1851 Great Exhibition, a structure built for showing things.

clue.text: See 21
Character's spoken with weavers offering family treasures

indicators.note: spoken means we use the sound of the word rather than its spelling

parts.note: character is air, as in an air of authority; the 's is just 'is'
looms are the machines that weave

explanation.surface: Someone talks to cloth-makers about inherited valuables.
explanation.walkthrough: AIR (character, manner) said aloud gives HEIR; looms do the weaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Heirlooms are valuable possessions handed down through generations of a family.

clue.text: Order parts for old wind instrument

indicators.note: parts for means the word splits open to make room for a letter

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: Someone orders spare parts for an antique woodwind.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind, blown by the player's breath.

clue.text: Couple in slavery

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to join or link together, as oxen are

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests two people in bondage; the words are two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A yoke is the wooden beam pairing oxen, and figuratively means servitude or subjugation.

clue.text: Mum reversing car always in Venezuelan city

parts.note: Ma is mum

indicators.note: reversing means the word car is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned round
ay is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Mother backs the car out in a South American town.
explanation.definitionFit: Maracay is a large city in northern Venezuela, capital of Aragua state.

clue.text: Chicken brought round in cargo helicopter

indicators.note: brought round means the first word is wrapped around the second

parts.note: chook is Australian slang for a chicken

explanation.surface: A hen is ferried in by a transport aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: CHOOK is Australian and New Zealand slang for a chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinook is the twin-rotor military transport helicopter built by Boeing.

clue.text: Cabal member Charlie succeeded in corrupt corporation

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in means this letter is placed within the rearranged letters
corrupt means the letters are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogy

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie climbed to the top of a crooked company and joined its conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeded' is S by the convention of family trees, where s. marks who succeeded whom.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabal is a secret plotting group, so each member is a fellow plotter alongside the others.

clue.text: Mysterious gain with climate fluctuating

indicators.note: fluctuating means varying, so the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzling increase that goes with a changing climate.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatical is a longer form of enigmatic: puzzling, obscure, hard to fathom.

clue.text: American name tag is held by a single needle

indicators.note: held by means the preceding word sits inside the next

parts.note: a single is one

explanation.surface: An American's name badge is pinned on with one needle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needle' looks like a sewing pin from the surface, but is the verb meaning to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or annoy them, the same as to antagonise.

clue.text: Gardeners working outside with verdant area

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters go round the other piece
working means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Gardeners are at work outdoors on a green patch.
explanation.walkthrough: GARDENERS is rearranged to GREENSARD, which goes around W.
explanation.definitionFit: Greensward is grassy turf, a stretch of lawn covered in green grass.

clue.text: Scientist fixes housing shortage at last, with partner secure

indicators.note: housing means holding something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: fixes means jams, as in getting into tight spots

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: its last letter is E
a love is a partner or sweetheart
to secure is to lock

explanation.surface: A report on someone who repairs housing shortages and has a reliable partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixes' is the noun, meaning tight spots, not the verb the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: James Lovelock was the British scientist and inventor who proposed the Gaia hypothesis.

clue.text: Like an endless rock and roll performance?

definitions.text: Like an endless rock and roll performance?

parts.words: Like an endless rock and roll performance?
parts.note: in Greek myth a king was condemned to roll a boulder uphill for ever, only for it to roll back down each time

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gig that never stops; read literally it is a rock being rolled for eternity, as Sisyphus did.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisyphean describes a task that is endless and futile, after the punishment of Sisyphus in the underworld.

clue.text: Laird fell into country road close to boozer

indicators.note: into means the first piece goes inside the next

parts.note: a lane is a country road
a fell is upland, as is a down

indicators.note: close to points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: its last letter is R

explanation.surface: A Scottish lord tumbled into a lane near the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landowner; fell and down are both words for open hilly land.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is the owner of a landed estate in Scotland, a proprietor of property.

clue.text: Dodgy dealer perhaps supplies instrument to comedians

indicators.note: to means the instrument is added on after the comedians

parts.note: cards are amusing, eccentric people
a harp is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: Someone provides a musical instrument for a comedy troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: A card is a comic character, so comedians are CARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp cheats at cards, so is a crooked dealer at the card table.

clue.text: Digger wants flat in Seascale vacated

indicators.note: in means the flat goes inside the remaining letters
vacated means emptied, so only the first and last letters remain

parts.note: a pad is a flat or apartment

explanation.surface: A digger is looking for an apartment in Seascale, a village on the Cumbrian coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A spade is a tool used for digging.

clue.text: Porridge is put out to trap adult rodents

indicators.note: to trap means the rearranged letters enclose the next piece
put out means disturbed, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Breakfast oats are set out as bait for grown-up vermin.
explanation.walkthrough: PORRIDGE IS rearranges to PRIRIEDOGS, which traps A.
explanation.definitionFit: Prairie dogs are burrowing North American ground squirrels, members of the rodent family.

clue.text: Butter, no good, sent out from Blighty

indicators.note: sent out from means these letters are removed from the following word

parts.note: Blighty is old British slang for England

explanation.surface: Spoiled butter is exported from Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' looks like the dairy spread, but it is something that butts with its horns.
explanation.definitionFit: An eland is a large African antelope, a horned animal that may butt.

clue.text: Powers should retain two articles in satellite? 1 Across's idea!

indicators.note: should retain means the first word keeps the other inside

parts.note: Gary Powers was the American U-2 spy-plane pilot shot down over the USSR

indicators.note: in means the articles go inside the satellite

parts.note: Io is a moon of Jupiter
a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: Powerful nations ought to keep a couple of items aboard a satellite, as the scientist proposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powers' looks like nations or forces, but is the surname of Gary Powers, the U-2 pilot; the satellite is a moon of Jupiter.
explanation.definitionFit: James Lovelock proposed the hypothesis that Earth behaves as a single self-regulating living system.

clue.text: Decline to answer question but get through

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to say '...' when unable to answer in a quiz
second meaning: to succeed in an exam

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests dodging a question yet still succeeding; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: In a quiz a contestant can skip a question, and a student can succeed in an exam; the same verb covers both.

clue.text: Answer arrived about French from universities

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word goes round the other

parts.note: came means arrived
de is French for from

explanation.surface: A reply turned up concerning French people from universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the academic world, the community of scholars and higher-education institutions.

clue.text: Empress keeps lethal gas in at back

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the other piece is placed inside
keeps in completes the idea of holding something inside
back means the word at is read backwards

parts.note: sarin is a lethal nerve gas

explanation.surface: An empress hoards a deadly gas somewhere in the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a Russian tsar, or a female ruler of Russia.

clue.text: Knight in virtue gives agreement

indicators.note: in means the knight's letter goes within the other word

parts.note: an asset is a good quality or virtue
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight's virtuous nature leads him to say yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent means consent or approval, an expression of accord.

clue.text: Connected when covering northern town

indicators.note: covering means the first word goes over the other piece

parts.note: bridged means connected, spanned

explanation.surface: Something was linked up while protecting a town in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridgend is a town in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridgend is a town in South Wales, a settlement giving its name to a county borough.
